question: All apples are fruits. All fruits are sweet. Which of the following is true?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. All apples are sweet.

GIVEN

• Statements: All apples are fruits. All fruits are sweet.

SOLUTION

• Draw a Venn diagram: the circle of "apples" lies completely inside the circle of "fruits", which lies completely inside the circle of "sweet things".

• So the circle of apples is completely inside the circle of sweet things: All apples are sweet.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• All A are B + All B are C ⟹ All A are C (the first rule of syllogism).

NOTE

• Option 2 (Some apples are sweet) is a weaker form of the sure conclusion; the direct conclusion of the two universal statements is "All apples are sweet", so this is not the answer asked for.

• Option 3 (No apple is sweet) is wrong: it contradicts the conclusion.

• Option 4 (Some fruits are apples) is also a true statement from the first statement (the converse of "All apples are fruits"), but it is not the conclusion drawn from both statements together.

FLAG

• Options 2 and 4 are also true statements; the PDF key (Option 1, the direct conclusion of both statements) has been followed.

question:
Statements:

1. All flowers are plants.

2. Some plants are trees.

Conclusions:

I. Some trees are flowers.

II. All flowers are trees.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Neither I nor II follows.

GIVEN

• Statements: 1. All flowers are plants (A-type). 2. Some plants are trees (I-type).

• Conclusions: I. Some trees are flowers. II. All flowers are trees.

SOLUTION

• Draw a Venn diagram: the circle of "flowers" is inside the circle of "plants". The circle of "trees" overlaps the circle of "plants", but it may overlap the "flowers" circle or may not, since the statement does not say which plants are trees.

• Conclusion I (Some trees are flowers): the trees may be in the part of plants outside the flowers circle, so it is not definite. It does not follow.

• Conclusion II (All flowers are trees): it is not definite either; the flowers may lie completely outside the trees. It does not follow.

• So neither I nor II follows.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• All A are B + Some B are C gives no definite conclusion (the middle term B is distributed only in the first premise as a predicate, not as a subject).

NOTE

• Option 1 (Only conclusion I follows) is wrong: "Some trees are flowers" is only a possibility, not a certainty.

• Option 2 (Only conclusion II follows) is wrong: "All flowers are trees" is not supported.

• Option 3 (Both I and II follow) is wrong: neither is definite.

question: Six students are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Amit is sitting second to the left of Jia. Jia is an immediate neighbour of both Varun and Pramod. Sia is sitting second to the left of Amit. Amit is an immediate neighbour of both Mahesh and Varun. Who is the immediate neighbour of Sia and Jia?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Pramod.

GIVEN

• Six students around a circular table facing the centre. Amit is 2nd to the left of Jia. Jia's neighbours: Varun and Pramod. Sia is 2nd to the left of Amit. Amit's neighbours: Mahesh and Varun.

SOLUTION

• (Facing the centre, "left" means the clockwise direction. Number the seats 0 to 5 clockwise.)

• Put Jia at seat 0. Amit is 2nd to the left of Jia, so Amit is at seat 2.

• Jia's neighbours (Varun and Pramod) occupy seats 1 and 5. Amit's neighbours (Mahesh and Varun) occupy seats 1 and 3. Varun is common to both, so Varun is at seat 1. Then Pramod is at seat 5 and Mahesh is at seat 3.

• The remaining person, Sia, sits at seat 4, which is 2nd to the left of Amit (seat 2 + 2 = 4) ✓.

• Seating (0 to 5): Jia, Varun, Amit, Mahesh, Sia, Pramod.

• Sia's neighbours are Mahesh and Pramod; Jia's neighbours are Varun and Pramod. The common neighbour is Pramod.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Find the person common to the two lists of neighbours: (Mahesh, Pramod) and (Varun, Pramod) → Pramod.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Varun) is wrong: he is a neighbour of Jia but not of Sia.

• Option 2 (Mahesh) is wrong: he is a neighbour of Sia but not of Jia.

• Option 4 (Amit) is wrong: he is not a neighbour of either Sia or Jia (he sits between Varun and Mahesh).

• Circular arrangement rule: facing the centre, left is clockwise and right is anticlockwise.

question: A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H are sitting around a circle facing the centre. F is third to the right of C and second to the left of H. D is not an immediate neighbour of C or H. E is on the immediate right of A, who is second to the right of G.Who sits between G and D?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. F.

GIVEN

• Eight persons sit around a circle facing the centre. F is 3rd to the right of C and 2nd to the left of H. D is not next to C or H. E is on the immediate right of A. A is 2nd to the right of G.

SOLUTION

• (Facing the centre, "right" is the anticlockwise direction. Number the seats 0 to 7 clockwise.)

• Put C at seat 0. F is 3rd to the right of C, so F is at seat 5. F is 2nd to the left of H, so H is at seat 3.

• D is not next to C (seats 1, 7) or H (seats 2, 4). The free seats are 1, 2, 4, 6, 7.

• E is on the immediate right of A, so E = A – 1. A is 2nd to the right of G, so G = A + 2.

• Try A = 7 and E = 6: then G = 1, and D and B would have to take seats 2 and 4, which are next to H, so D cannot sit there. This is not possible.

• Try A = 2 and E = 1: then G = 4, and D and B take seats 6 and 7. D cannot be at seat 7 (next to C), so D = 6 and B = 7.

• Seating (0 to 7): C, E, A, H, G, F, D, B.

• Between G (seat 4) and D (seat 6) is seat 5, which is F.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Fix C, F and H first, then use the "D is not a neighbour of C or H" condition to eliminate the second possibility. G and D are two seats apart, so only one person sits between them.

NOTE

• Option 2 (H) is wrong: H sits at seat 3, next to G on the other side.

• Option 3 (E) is wrong: E sits at seat 1, far from G and D.

• Option 4 (D) is wrong: D is one of the two persons named in the question, not the one between them.

• Circular arrangement rule: facing the centre, the person on your right is in the anticlockwise direction.

question: At what time between 4 and 5 o'clock will the minute hand and the hour hand be exactly opposite to each other?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. None of the mentioned.

GIVEN

• Between 4 and 5 o'clock, the hands are opposite (180° apart).

SOLUTION

• At 4 o'clock, the hour hand is 120° ahead of the minute hand (at 12). The minute hand must be 180° ahead of the hour hand, so it has to gain 120° + 180° = 300°.

• The minute hand gains 5.5° per minute (6° – 0.5°). Time = 300 ÷ 5.5 = 600/11 = 54 6/11 minutes past 4.

• This is not any of the first three options, so the answer is None of the mentioned.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Formula for the hands to be opposite between h and h + 1: minutes = (5h + 30) × 12/11 for h < 6, i.e. (20 + 30) × 12/11 = 600/11 = 54 6/11.

NOTE

• Option 1 (16 minutes past 4): at about 16 4/11 minutes the hands are together (coincide), not opposite. At 16 minutes the minute hand is at 96° and the hour hand at 128°.

• Option 2 (18 minutes past 4): the hour hand is at 129° and the minute hand at 108°; they are 21° apart, not 180°.

• Option 3 (22 minutes past 4): the hour hand is at 131° and the minute hand at 132°; they are almost together, not opposite.

• Clock facts: the minute hand moves 6° per minute; the hour hand moves 0.5° per minute; the hands coincide 11 times, and are opposite 11 times in 12 hours.

question:
Arrange the following words in the order they appear in the dictionary:

 

1. Intense

2. Intellect

3. Intend

4. Intelligent

5. Intensity
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 2, 4, 3, 1, 5.

GIVEN

• Words: 1. Intense, 2. Intellect, 3. Intend, 4. Intelligent, 5. Intensity.

SOLUTION

• All the words begin with "Inte". Look at the next letters: "l" (Intellect, Intelligent) comes before "n" (Intend, Intense, Intensity).

• Between Intellect and Intelligent: they are the same up to "Intell", then "e" (Intellect) comes before "i" (Intelligent). So Intellect, then Intelligent.

• Between Intend, Intense and Intensity: "Inten" is common. The next letters are "d" (Intend), "s" (Intense, Intensity). So Intend comes first.

• Intense and Intensity: "Intens" is common, then "e" (Intense) comes before "i" (Intensity).

• Order: Intellect (2), Intelligent (4), Intend (3), Intense (1), Intensity (5), i.e. 2, 4, 3, 1, 5.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Compare letter by letter from the left. The first difference decides: l < n, e < i, d < s.

NOTE

• Option 1 (5, 1, 3, 2, 4) is wrong: Intensity and Intense cannot come before Intellect (l comes before n).

• Option 3 (5, 3, 2, 4, 1) is wrong: Intensity is placed first, but "Intellect" must come before any "Inten…" word.

• Option 4 (2, 4, 1, 3, 5) is wrong: Intense (1) is placed before Intend (3), but "d" comes before "s".

• Dictionary order rule: compare letters from left to right; a shorter word that is the beginning of a longer word comes first (e.g. Intense before Intensity).

question:
After interchanging which two numbers (not digits) will the value of the expression become 81?

798 + 27 – 719 ÷ 6 × 5
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 798 and 719.

GIVEN

• Expression: 798 + 27 – 719 ÷ 6 × 5. After interchanging two numbers, the value must be 81.

SOLUTION

• Test Option 2 (interchange 798 and 719): 719 + 27 – 798 ÷ 6 × 5.

• By BODMAS: 798 ÷ 6 = 133; 133 × 5 = 665.

• 719 + 27 = 746; 746 – 665 = 81 ✓.

• So the numbers to be interchanged are 798 and 719.

question: Look at the matrix and choose the number from the options that should go in place of the question mark:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 56.

GIVEN

• Matrix: row 1 = 6, 18, 42; row 2 = 5, 15, 35; row 3 = 8, 24, ?.

SOLUTION

• In each row, the second number = 3 × the first number: 6 × 3 = 18; 5 × 3 = 15; 8 × 3 = 24.

• In each row, the third number = 7 × the first number: 6 × 7 = 42; 5 × 7 = 35.

• So in row 3, ? = 8 × 7 = 56.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Divide the third number by the first in the complete rows: 42 ÷ 6 = 7 and 35 ÷ 5 = 7. Then 8 × 7 = 56.

NOTE

• Option 1 (42) is wrong: it is the value in the first row and does not equal 8 × 7.

• Option 3 (24) is wrong: it is the second number of the same row, and does not equal 8 × 7.

• Option 4 (16) is wrong: it equals 8 × 2, which does not match the rule.

• Always check the rule in every complete row (or column) before using it for the missing number.

question: In a certain code language, ‘bright red lamp’ is written as ‘ki po ru’, ‘red green wall’ is written as ‘po la mi’ and ‘lamp wall door’ is written as ‘ru mi ta’. What is the code for ‘green’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. la.

GIVEN

• bright red lamp = ki po ru; red green wall = po la mi; lamp wall door = ru mi ta.

SOLUTION

• "red" is common to the first two statements, and "po" is the common code, so red = po.

• "lamp" is common to the first and third statements, and "ru" is the common code, so lamp = ru.

• "wall" is common to the second and third statements, and "mi" is the common code, so wall = mi.

• In the second statement (red green wall = po la mi), after removing red = po and wall = mi, the remaining code "la" stands for green. So green = la.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Find the word and the code that repeat in two statements. After removing the known pairs, the leftover word and the leftover code match.

NOTE

• Option 1 (po) is wrong: po is the code for "red".

• Option 3 (mi) is wrong: mi is the code for "wall".

• Option 4 (ru) is wrong: ru is the code for "lamp".

question: What does elasticity of demand measures?

question: What is the significance of Lagrange points in space missions?

• Option 3 (Has been abolished) is wrong: it has been kept in the new law.

 

• Option 4 (Applies only in civil cases) is wrong: the Evidence law applies to both civil and criminal proceedings.

 

EXTRA FACTS

 

• The three new criminal laws in force from 1 July 2024: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (replaces the IPC), Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (replaces the CrPC) and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (replaces the Evidence Act).

question: What is the status of burden of proof under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA)?
option_1: It applies only in civil cases.
option_3: It is always on the accused.
option_4: It primarily lies on the prosecution but may shift in specific circumstances.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It primarily lies on the prosecution but may shift in specific circumstances..

 

ANSWER

 

• It primarily lies on the prosecution but may shift in specific circumstances.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

EXPLANATION

 

• Under the BSA (as under the old Evidence Act), the burden of proof lies on the person who asserts a fact (Sections 104–106 BSA, formerly 101–103). In criminal cases the burden rests on the prosecution to prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt, but in specific cases (for example, special exceptions, or facts specially within the knowledge of the accused) the burden shifts to the accused.

 

WHY THE OTHERS ARE WRONG

 

• Option 1 (It applies only in civil cases) is wrong: burden of proof applies in criminal cases too.

 

• Option 2 (It never shifts during trial) is wrong: the evidential burden can shift, as in statutory presumptions.

 

• Option 3 (It is always on the accused) is wrong: an accused is presumed innocent until proved guilty.

 

EXTRA FACTS

 

• "He who asserts must prove" is the basic rule. The BSA has 170 sections, against 167 in the Indian Evidence Act, and expressly recognises electronic records as documentary evidence.

question: Which combination best describes the spatial pattern of India’s major coal, petroleum, and natural gas resources?
option_1: Coal everywhere; petroleum only Thar Desert; gas in Indo-Gangetic Plain
option_2: Coal only Himalayas; petroleum in plateaus; gas in south river deltas
option_3: Coal, petroleum, gas in one belt (Gujarat → West Bengal)
option_4: Coal in east/central India; petroleum off west coast & Assam; gas with onshore/offshore petroleum
solution_text:
The correct answer is Coal in east/central India; petroleum off west coast & Assam; gas with onshore/offshore petroleum.

 

ANSWER

 

• Coal in east/central India; petroleum off west coast & Assam; gas with onshore/offshore petroleum.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

EXPLANATION

 

• Most coal is in the Gondwana fields of Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh. Petroleum is found at Mumbai High (off the west coast), Gujarat and Assam (Digboi, Naharkatia). Natural gas occurs mostly with petroleum (associated gas), e.g. Mumbai High and the Krishna-Godavari basin.

 

WHY THE OTHERS ARE WRONG

 

• Option 1 is wrong: coal is not found everywhere, and petroleum is not confined to the Thar Desert (it is only a minor field there).

 

• Option 2 is wrong: the Himalayas have little coal (only small Tertiary deposits), and petroleum is not mainly in the plateaus.

 

• Option 3 is wrong: the three resources do not lie in one single belt from Gujarat to West Bengal.

 

EXTRA FACTS

 

• Digboi (Assam) is India's oldest oil field (1889). Jharia (Jharkhand) is the main coking coal field. Gondwana coal accounts for about 98 per cent of India's coal reserves.

question: What is the result of: (10 + 2) × (6 - 4) ÷ 2?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 12.

GIVEN

• Expression: (10 + 2) × (6 − 4) ÷ 2.

SOLUTION

• Brackets first: (10 + 2) = 12 and (6 − 4) = 2.

• Then × and ÷ from left to right: 12 × 2 = 24; 24 ÷ 2 = 12.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• The "× 2 ÷ 2" cancel each other, leaving 12.

NOTE

• Option 1 (6) is wrong: it does not equal 12 × 2 ÷ 2 = 12 (it would result only from dividing 12 by 2 and forgetting the factor 2).

• Option 3 (10) is wrong: it does not equal 12 × 2 ÷ 2.

• Option 4 (8) is wrong: it does not equal 12 × 2 ÷ 2.

• Rule: BODMAS (Brackets, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction); × and ÷ are done left to right.

question: A shopkeeper combines two qualities of tea, one at Rs.75/kg and the other at Rs.105/kg, in the ratio of 3:2. Calculate the cost price per kg of this tea mixture.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Rs.87/kg.

GIVEN

• Quality 1: Rs.75/kg; Quality 2: Rs.105/kg; ratio of mixing = 3 : 2.

SOLUTION

• Total cost of 5 kg = 3 × 75 + 2 × 105 = 225 + 210 = Rs.435.

• Cost per kg = 435 ÷ 5 = Rs.87/kg.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Weighted mean: 75 + (2/5) × (105 − 75) = 75 + 12 = 87.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Rs.89/kg) is wrong: it is not the weighted mean 435 ÷ 5.

• Option 2 (Rs.97/kg) is wrong: it is not the weighted mean 435 ÷ 5.

• Option 3 (Rs.77/kg) is wrong: it is not the weighted mean 435 ÷ 5.

• Formula: mean price = (n₁p₁ + n₂p₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

question: The next term in the series 1, 4, 36, 576, ….. is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 14400.

GIVEN

• Series: 1, 4, 36, 576, ……

SOLUTION

• The terms are perfect squares: 1 = 1², 4 = 2², 36 = 6², 576 = 24².

• The bases 1, 2, 6, 24 are the factorials 1!, 2!, 3!, 4!.

• The next base is 5! = 120, so the next term = 120² = 14400.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Spot the squares, then the base pattern 1, 2, 6, 24 (each base is multiplied by 2, 3, 4, then 5).

NOTE

• Option 1 (3600) is wrong: it is 60², and 60 is not 5!.

• Option 2 (8100) is wrong: it is 90², and 90 is not 5!.

• Option 3 (12100) is wrong: it is 110², and 110 is not 5!. (The PDF shows this option as a wrong selection.)

• Remember: n! = 1, 2, 6, 24, 120, 720 for n = 1 to 6.

question: A gardener plants some trees in the form of a perfect rectangle. The number of trees in each row is 6 more than the number of rows. If the total number of trees planted is 135, find the number of rows?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 9.

GIVEN

• Trees in each row = rows + 6; total trees = 135.

SOLUTION

• Let the number of rows be x. Then x(x + 6) = 135.

• x² + 6x − 135 = 0, i.e. (x + 15)(x − 9) = 0, so x = 9 (the negative value is rejected).

• Check: 9 × 15 = 135. Number of rows = 9.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Find two factors of 135 that differ by 6: 9 and 15. The smaller one is the number of rows.

NOTE

• Option 1 (8) is wrong: 8 × 14 = 112, not 135.

• Option 3 (7) is wrong: 7 × 13 = 91, not 135.

• Option 4 (2) is wrong: 2 × 8 = 16, not 135.

question: A sum of money becomes Rs. 47,600 at compound interest. If rate of interest in three years is 11.11%, 16.66%, 12.5% respectively. Find the compound interest?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Rs. 14,960.

GIVEN

• Amount after 3 years = Rs. 47,600; rates are 11.11% = 1/9, 16.66% = 1/6 and 12.5% = 1/8 for the three years.

SOLUTION

• Growth factors: 10/9, 7/6, 9/8.

• Product = (10 × 7 × 9) ÷ (9 × 6 × 8) = 630 ÷ 432 = 35/24.

• Principal = 47,600 × 24/35 = 1,360 × 24 = Rs. 32,640.

• Compound interest = 47,600 − 32,640 = Rs. 14,960.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Convert the percentages into fractions (11.11% = 1/9, 16.66% = 1/6, 12.5% = 1/8). The amount is 35/24 of the principal, so the principal is 24 parts and the interest is 11 parts; 11 × 1,360 = 14,960.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Rs. 13,360) is wrong: it does not equal 47,600 − 32,640.

• Option 2 (Rs. 15,000) is wrong: it does not equal 47,600 − 32,640.

• Option 4 (Rs. 17,560) is wrong: it does not equal 47,600 − 32,640. (The PDF shows this option as a wrong selection.)

• Remember: 1/9 = 11.11%, 1/6 = 16.66%, 1/8 = 12.5%, 1/7 = 14.28%.

question: A shopkeeper marks an article at a price such that after giving discount of 20% and he gains k%. If the cost price and the marked price of the article are Rs. 4,400 and Rs. 6,500 respectively. What is the value of k?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 18.18%.

GIVEN

• Cost price = Rs. 4,400; marked price = Rs. 6,500; discount = 20%; gain = k%.

SOLUTION

• Selling price = 80% of 6,500 = Rs. 5,200.

• Gain = 5,200 − 4,400 = Rs. 800.

• k = (800 ÷ 4,400) × 100 = 200/11 = 18.18%.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• SP = 0.8 × 6,500 = 5,200; gain/CP = 800/4,400 = 2/11 = 18.18%.

NOTE

• Option 1 (25%) is wrong: it would need SP = 5,500.

• Option 2 (16.25%) is wrong: it would need SP = Rs. 5,115, but SP = 80% of 6,500 = Rs. 5,200.

• Option 4 (14.75%) is wrong: it would need SP ≈ Rs. 5,049.

• Formula: Gain % = (SP − CP) ÷ CP × 100.

question: A can has a capacity of 300 liters and it is completely filled with pure milk. From this can, 30 liters of milk is removed and the same amount (30 liters) of water is added to fill the can again. This process of removing 30 liters of the mixture and replacing it with 30 liters of water is repeated several times. After repeating the process a certain number of times, the quantity of pure milk left in the can reduces to 218.7 liters. How many times must this process be carried out for the amount of pure milk to become 218.7 liters?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 3.

GIVEN

• Capacity 300 L, replaced each time 30 L; final milk = 218.7 L.

SOLUTION

• Milk left after n operations = 300 × (1 − 30/300)ⁿ = 300 × (0.9)ⁿ.

• 300 × (0.9)ⁿ = 218.7, so (0.9)ⁿ = 0.729 = (0.9)³.

• Hence n = 3.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Multiply 300 by 0.9 repeatedly: 270 → 243 → 218.7. Three steps.

NOTE

• Option 1 (2) is wrong: after 2 operations the milk is 243 L.

• Option 3 (4) is wrong: after 4 operations the milk is 196.83 L.

• Option 4 (5) is wrong: after 5 operations the milk is 177.1 L (approx.).

• Formula: milk left = V × (1 − x/V)ⁿ.

question: A company deploys 500 labourers to restore an old fort wall. In the first 15 weeks, they manage to rebuild 2/5 of the total structure. Suddenly, a severe storm hits the region, causing the restoration work to be stopped for 6 weeks. During this period of inactivity, 1/2 of the portion already restored collapses due to the storm damage. When the weather clears and the restoration resumes, only 360 labourers return to work. Assuming that no further interruptions occur, in how many weeks from the beginning will the entire restoration project be completed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 62.67 weeks.

GIVEN

• 500 labourers do 2/5 of the work in 15 weeks; 6 weeks stoppage; 1/2 of the restored part collapses; 360 labourers resume.

SOLUTION

• After the collapse, work done = 2/5 × 1/2 = 1/5, so remaining work = 1 − 1/5 = 4/5.

• Work rate: 500 labourers do 2/5 in 15 weeks, so 500 × 15 = 7,500 labourer-weeks give 2/5. Whole work = 18,750 labourer-weeks.

• Remaining work 4/5 needs 4/5 × 18,750 = 15,000 labourer-weeks.

• Time with 360 labourers = 15,000 ÷ 360 = 41.67 weeks.

• Total time from the beginning = 15 + 6 + 41.67 = 62.67 weeks. Answer: 62.67 weeks.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Total = 18,750 man-weeks; remaining 15,000 ÷ 360 = 41.67; add 15 + 6 = 21, giving 62.67.

NOTE

• Option 1 (42.33 weeks) is wrong: it ignores the 15 weeks before and the 6 weeks of stoppage.

• Option 2 (57.23 weeks) is wrong: it does not follow from the working above.

• Option 4 (55.25 weeks) is wrong: it does not follow from the working above.

• Formula: work = labourers × time (man-weeks).

question: A man begins his trip 36 minutes later than his regular starting time. To make up for the delay, he travels at 180% of his usual speed and ends up reaching his destination 16 minutes earlier than his usual arrival time. Find the usual time taken for the journey?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 117 minutes.

GIVEN

• Late start = 36 min; new speed = 180% = 9/5 of usual speed; arrival = 16 min earlier than usual.

SOLUTION

• Let the usual time be T minutes. The new journey time = T ÷ 1.8 = 5T/9.

• He starts 36 min late and arrives 16 min early, so the new journey time = T − (36 + 16) = T − 52.

• 5T/9 = T − 52, so 4T/9 = 52 and T = 52 × 9/4 = 117 minutes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Time saved = 36 + 16 = 52 min. Speed ratio 9 : 5 means time ratio 5 : 9, so 4 parts = 52 and 9 parts = 117.

NOTE

• Option 1 (95 minutes) is wrong: new time 52.8 min would not give a saving of 52 min (95 − 52.8 = 42.2).

• Option 3 (104 minutes) is wrong: saving would be 104 − 57.8 = 46.2 min, not 52.

• Option 4 (119 minutes) is wrong: saving would be 119 − 66.1 = 52.9 min, not 52.

• Formula: when speed is increased in the ratio a : b, the time changes in the ratio b : a.

question: A train going from P to Q, meets an accident after travelling 90 km. Due to the accident, the train reduces its speed to 2/3 of its normal speed and reaches its destination 30 minutes late, had the same accident occurred 60 km further the train would have reached the same destination just 10 min late. What is the distance from P to Q?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 180 km.

GIVEN

• Accident after 90 km; new speed = 2/3 of normal; delay = 30 min. Accident 60 km further (after 150 km): delay = 10 min.

SOLUTION

• Let the normal speed be v km/min. For the distance x after the accident, the extra time = x ÷ (2v/3) − x/v = 3x/2v − x/v = x/(2v).

• Case 1: (D − 90)/(2v) = 30. Case 2: (D − 150)/(2v) = 10.

• Subtracting: 60/(2v) = 20, so v = 1.5 km/min (90 km/h).

• D − 90 = 30 × 2 × 1.5 = 90, so D = 180 km.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Delay difference 20 min comes from 60 km, so 1 min of delay = 3 km. Then 30 min delay = 90 km after the accident, so D = 90 + 90 = 180 km.

NOTE

• Option 1 (170 km) is wrong: the delay after 90 km would then be 80 km ÷ 3 = 26.7 min, not 30.

• Option 3 (210 km) is wrong: the delay would be 120 ÷ 3 = 40 min, not 30.

• Option 4 (190 km) is wrong: the delay would be 100 ÷ 3 = 33.3 min, not 30.

• Formula: at 2/3 speed the time taken becomes 3/2 times, i.e. an extra half of the normal time.

• Source note: in the PDF, a page break falls between option 2 and option 3; the question has four options.

question: Three men can build a wall individually in 12 hours, 15 hours and 20 hours, respectively. However, if they work together, they end up using 340 fewer bricks per hour than the sum of their individual rates and complete the wall in 15 hours. Find the total number of bricks in the wall?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 2550.

GIVEN

• Individual times 12 h, 15 h, 20 h; together they lay 340 fewer bricks per hour than the sum of the individual rates and take 15 hours.

SOLUTION

• Let the number of bricks be N. Sum of individual rates = N/12 + N/15 + N/20 = N(5 + 4 + 3)/60 = N/5 per hour.

• Together rate = N/15 per hour (the wall is done in 15 hours).

• N/5 − N/15 = 340, so 2N/15 = 340 and N = 340 × 15/2 = 2,550 bricks.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Sum of rates = 1/5 and actual rate = 1/15; the difference 2/15 of the wall = 340 bricks, so the wall = 340 × 7.5 = 2,550.

NOTE

• Option 1 (2700) is wrong: 2/15 of 2,700 = 360, not 340.

• Option 2 (3250) is wrong: 2/15 of 3,250 ≈ 433, not 340.

• Option 4 (3200) is wrong: 2/15 of 3,200 ≈ 427, not 340.

• Formula: work = rate × time; combined rate = sum of individual rates when there is no loss.

question: In a circle, two chords AB and CD are equal in length. If chord AB subtends an angle of 35° at the centre, find the angle subtended by chord CD at the centre.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 35°.

GIVEN

• Chords AB = CD; angle subtended by AB at the centre = 35°.

SOLUTION

• Equal chords of a circle subtend equal angles at the centre.

• So the angle subtended by CD = 35°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Equal chords means equal central angles, so copy the angle: 35°.

NOTE

• Option 1 (30°) is wrong: it is not equal to the angle subtended by AB.

• Option 3 (40°) is wrong: it is not equal to the angle subtended by AB.

• Option 4 (70°) is wrong: it is double the angle (the 2θ relation applies to the angle at the circumference, and here both angles are at the centre).

• Theorem: equal chords are equidistant from the centre and subtend equal angles at the centre.

question: If y =  + 1, then the value of 1 +  (1/y) + (1/y²) − (1/y³) + (1/y⁴) − (1/y⁵) is?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 2.

• y = +1; the expression is 1 + (1/y) + (1/y²) − (1/y³) + (1/y⁴) − (1/y⁵).

SOLUTION

• With y = 1, every power of 1/y equals 1.

• Value = 1 + 1 + 1 − 1 + 1 − 1 = 2.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

• All the terms equal 1, so count the signs: four plus (1 each, including the leading 1) and two minus gives 2.

question: A, B and C invest ₹24,000, ₹36,000 and ₹12,000 respectively in a business. A is the working partner and receives 26.67% of the total profit for managing the business. The remaining profit is shared among A, B and C in the ratio of their capitals. At the end of the year, A’s total share of profit ₹300 more than the combined shares of B and C. Find the amount that gets by A?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. ₹6,900.

GIVEN

• Capitals ₹24,000 : ₹36,000 : ₹12,000 = 2 : 3 : 1. A gets 26.67% = 4/15 of the total profit as a managing fee. A's total share exceeds B + C combined by ₹300.

SOLUTION

• Let the total profit be P. Managing share of A = 4P/15. Remaining = 11P/15, shared 2 : 3 : 1 (total 6 parts).

• A's share of the remainder = (2/6) × 11P/15 = 11P/45. A's total = 12P/45 + 11P/45 = 23P/45.

• B + C = (4/6) × 11P/15 = 22P/45.

• Difference = 23P/45 − 22P/45 = P/45 = ₹300, so P = ₹13,500.

• A's share = 23 × 300 = ₹6,900.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Take P = 45 units: A = 23 units, B + C = 22 units. The difference of 1 unit = ₹300, so A = 23 × 300 = ₹6,900.

NOTE

• Option 1 (₹7,500) is wrong: it is not 23 units of ₹300 (it would mean 25 units).

• Option 2 (₹6,500) is wrong: it is not 23 units of ₹300.

• Option 4 (₹5,600) is wrong: it is not 23 units of ₹300.

• Remember: 26.67% = 4/15, 33.33% = 1/3, 16.67% = 1/6.

question: If √(8ⁿ) = 512, then the value of n is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 6.

GIVEN

• √(8ⁿ) = 512.

SOLUTION

• 512 = 8³, so 8^(n/2) = 8³.

• Equating powers: n/2 = 3, so n = 6.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Square both sides: 8ⁿ = 512² = 8⁶, so n = 6.

NOTE

• Option 1 (8) is wrong: √(8⁸) = 8⁴ = 4,096, not 512.

• Option 2 (3) is wrong: √(8³) = √512 ≈ 22.6, not 512. (The PDF shows this option as a wrong selection.)

• Option 3 (4) is wrong: √(8⁴) = 8² = 64, not 512.

• Powers of 8: 8 = 8¹, 64 = 8², 512 = 8³, 4,096 = 8⁴.

question: In ΔABC, a line DE is drawn parallel to BC, meeting AB at D and AC at E. If AD:DB = 2:3 and BC = 35 cm, find DE.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 14 cm.

GIVEN

• DE ∥ BC; AD : DB = 2 : 3; BC = 35 cm.

SOLUTION

• AD : AB = 2 : (2 + 3) = 2 : 5.

• Triangles ADE and ABC are similar, so DE/BC = AD/AB = 2/5.

• DE = (2/5) × 35 = 14 cm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Add the ratio parts to get AB = 5 parts; DE = 2/5 of BC = 14 cm.

NOTE

• Option 1 (12 cm) is wrong: it is not 2/5 of 35.

• Option 3 (16 cm) is wrong: it is not 2/5 of 35.

• Option 4 (21 cm) is wrong: it is 3/5 of 35, which comes from using DB instead of AD.

• Theorem: a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides in the same ratio (Basic Proportionality Theorem).

question: A is twice as efficient as B, and B is 50% more efficient than C. If A, B and C together complete a work in 12 days, in how many days can B alone complete the work?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 44 days.

GIVEN

• A = 2B; B = 1.5C; A, B and C together take 12 days.

SOLUTION

• B : C = 3 : 2 and A : B = 2 : 1 = 6 : 3, so A : B : C = 6 : 3 : 2 (total 11 units per day).

• Total work = 11 × 12 = 132 units.

• B's days = 132 ÷ 3 = 44 days.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Make B equal in both ratios (3), then B alone = total work ÷ B's units = 132 ÷ 3 = 44.

NOTE

• Option 1 (36 days) is wrong: it would need B's efficiency to be 3.67 units.

• Option 2 (40 days) is wrong: 132 ÷ 40 is not a whole number of units.

• Option 3 (49 days) is wrong: 132 ÷ 49 is not a whole number of units.

• Formula: total work = efficiency × days.

• Source note: in the PDF, a page break falls between option 1 and option 2; the question has four options.

question: A trapezium has parallel sides 18 cm and 32 cm. The distance between the parallel sides is 10 cm. What is the area of the trapezium?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 250 cm².

GIVEN

• Parallel sides 18 cm and 32 cm; height = 10 cm.

SOLUTION

• Area = ½ × (sum of parallel sides) × height = ½ × (18 + 32) × 10 = ½ × 50 × 10 = 250 cm².

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Average of the parallel sides = 25; 25 × 10 = 250.

NOTE

• Option 1 (220 cm²) is wrong: it does not equal ½ × 50 × 10.

• Option 2 (240 cm²) is wrong: it does not equal ½ × 50 × 10.

• Option 4 (300 cm²) is wrong: it does not equal ½ × 50 × 10 (the factor ½ is required).

• Formula: area of a trapezium = ½ (a + b) h.

question: The diagonals of a rhombus are in the ratio 11:60 and its perimeter is 244 cm. What is its area?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 1320 cm².

GIVEN

• Diagonals d₁ : d₂ = 11 : 60; perimeter = 244 cm.

SOLUTION

• Side = 244 ÷ 4 = 61 cm.

• Let the diagonals be 11k and 60k. The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, so side² = (11k/2)² + (60k/2)², giving 61² = (k/2)² × (121 + 3,600) = (k/2)² × 3,721 = (k/2)² × 61².

• So k/2 = 1, and k = 2. Diagonals = 22 cm and 120 cm.

• Area = ½ × 22 × 120 = 1,320 cm².

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• 11, 60, 61 is a Pythagorean triplet, so half-diagonals are 11 and 60 with side 61: the diagonals are 22 and 120. Area = ½ × 22 × 120 = 1,320.

NOTE

• Option 1 (1200 cm²) is wrong: it does not equal ½ × 22 × 120.

• Option 3 (1440 cm²) is wrong: it does not equal ½ × 22 × 120.

• Option 4 (1560 cm²) is wrong: it does not equal ½ × 22 × 120.

• Formula: area of a rhombus = ½ × d₁ × d₂.

question: A 12 m high tree casts a shadow of length 12√3 m. Find the angle of elevation of the sun.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 30°.

GIVEN

• Height of tree = 12 m; shadow length = 12√3 m.

SOLUTION

• tan θ = height ÷ shadow = 12 ÷ 12√3 = 1/√3.

• tan 30° = 1/√3, so θ = 30°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Height : shadow = 1 : √3 is the 30°–60°–90° triangle; the angle opposite the shorter side (height) is 30°.

NOTE

• Option 2 (45°) is wrong: tan 45° = 1, which needs shadow = height.

question: From the roof of a 20 m high building, the angle of elevation of the top of a tower is 45° and the angle of depression of its foot is 30°. Find the height of the tower.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 20(√3 + 1) m.

GIVEN

• Building height = 20 m; angle of depression of the foot of the tower = 30°; angle of elevation of the top of the tower from the roof = 45°.

SOLUTION

• Distance between the building and the tower = 20 ÷ tan 30° = 20√3 m.

• Height of the tower above the roof = 20√3 × tan 45° = 20√3 m.

• Total height of the tower = 20 + 20√3 = 20(√3 + 1) m.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• The base distance 20√3 is also the part above the roof (tan 45° = 1), so height = 20 + 20√3.

NOTE

• Option 1 (20√3 m) is wrong: it is only the part of the tower above the roof level.

• Option 3 (40√3 m) is wrong: it doubles 20√3 and ignores the 20 m of the building.

• Option 4 (20(2√3 + 1) m) is wrong: it is 20 + 40√3, which has an extra 20√3.

• Remember: angles of elevation and depression are measured from the horizontal.

solution_text:

question: A set is formed as S = (−2, 0, ¾, √16, √15). Under the usual school convention where natural numbers start from 1, how many elements of S are natural numbers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 1.

GIVEN

• S = {−2, 0, ¾, √16, √15}; natural numbers N = {1, 2, 3, …}.

SOLUTION

• −2 is a negative integer, so it is not natural. 0 is not natural (the convention starts from 1).

• ¾ is a fraction, so it is not natural.

• √16 = 4, which is a natural number.

• √15 ≈ 3.87 is irrational, so it is not natural.

• Only one element (√16 = 4) is natural. Answer: 1.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Simplify each root first: √16 = 4 is natural; √15 is not a perfect square, so it is irrational.

NOTE

• Option 2 (2) is wrong: it counts 0 as natural, but the question says natural numbers start from 1.

• Option 3 (3) is wrong: only one element qualifies.

• Option 4 (4) is wrong: only one element qualifies.

• Remember: natural numbers N = {1, 2, 3, …}; whole numbers W = {0, 1, 2, …}.

question: A rational number has a terminating decimal expansion only when the denominator in lowest terms has no prime factors other than 2 and 5. Which fraction below has a non-terminating recurring decimal expansion?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 7/12.

GIVEN

• A fraction terminates only if its lowest-terms denominator has no prime factor other than 2 and 5.

SOLUTION

• 13/40: 40 = 2³ × 5, so it terminates (0.325).

• 7/12: 12 = 2² × 3, which has the prime factor 3, so it is non-terminating and recurring (0.58333…).

• 21/28 = 3/4: the denominator 4 = 2², so it terminates (0.75).

• 25/125 = 1/5: the denominator 5, so it terminates (0.2).

• Answer: 7/12.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Reduce each fraction first, then look at the denominator: only 12 has a factor of 3.

NOTE

• Option 1 (13/40) is wrong: 40 = 2³ × 5, so the decimal terminates.

• Option 3 (21/28) is wrong: it reduces to 3/4 = 0.75, which terminates.

• Option 4 (25/125) is wrong: it reduces to 1/5 = 0.2, which terminates.

• Always reduce to lowest terms before applying the rule.

question: If sin⁴θ + cos⁴θ = 7/9, then find tan²θ + cot²θ.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 7.

GIVEN

• sin⁴θ + cos⁴θ = 7/9.

SOLUTION

• sin⁴θ + cos⁴θ = (sin²θ + cos²θ)² − 2 sin²θ cos²θ = 1 − 2 sin²θ cos²θ.

• So 1 − 2 sin²θ cos²θ = 7/9, giving 2 sin²θ cos²θ = 2/9 and sin²θ cos²θ = 1/9.

• tan²θ + cot²θ = (sin⁴θ + cos⁴θ) ÷ (sin²θ cos²θ) = (7/9) ÷ (1/9) = 7.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• tan²θ + cot²θ = (sin⁴θ + cos⁴θ) ÷ (sin²θ cos²θ), so divide 7/9 by 1/9 to get 7.

NOTE

• Option 1 (5) is wrong: it does not equal (7/9) ÷ (1/9).

• Option 2 (6) is wrong: it does not equal (7/9) ÷ (1/9).

• Option 4 (8) is wrong: it does not equal (7/9) ÷ (1/9).

• Identity: a² + b² = (a + b)² − 2ab, here with a = sin²θ and b = cos²θ.

question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

The teacher said, "We will go for a picnic tomorrow."
option_1: The teacher said that they would go for a picnic tomorrow.
option_2: The teacher said that they would go for a picnic the next day.
option_3: The teacher said that we will go for a picnic the next day.
option_4: The teacher said that they will go for a picnic the following day.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The teacher said that they would go for a picnic the next day..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In indirect speech with a past reporting verb ("said"), the tense moves back: "will" → "would"; the pronoun "we" → "they" (the speaker is the teacher, speaking about the class group); the time word "tomorrow" → "the next day" or "the following day".

◦ Direct: The teacher said, "We will go for a picnic tomorrow." → Indirect: The teacher said that they would go for a picnic the next day.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: wrong — "tomorrow" should change to "the next day" (the reporting verb is in the past).

 

• Option 3: wrong — "will" should change to "would", and "we" to "they".

 

• Option 4: wrong — "will" should change to "would" after the past reporting verb, even though "the following day" is right.

 

NOTE

 

• Changes of time words: today → that day; tomorrow → the next day / the following day; yesterday → the previous day; now → then; last week → the previous week.

question:
The sentences of a passage have been shuffled and labelled P, Q, R, and S. Rearrange these sentences to form the most logically coherent and meaningful paragraph. Choose the correct sequence from the options provided.

 

P: Shortly after this, he was accused of complicity in an abortive conspiracy against the Medici, imprisoned, and put to the question by torture.

 

Q: On the return of the Medici, Machiavelli, who for a few weeks had vainly hoped to retain his office under the new masters of Florence, was dismissed by decree dated 7th November 1512.

 

R: He has left a very interesting description of his life at this period, which elucidates his methods and his motives in writing “The Prince” in a letter to Francesco Vettor.

 

S: The new Medicean pope, Leo X, procured his release, and he retired to his small property at San Casciano, near Florence, where he devoted himself to literature.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. QPSR.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Find the opening sentence first: Q begins the account (the Medici return and Machiavelli is dismissed in November 1512).

 

• P follows ("Shortly after this" refers to the dismissal): he is accused, imprisoned and tortured.

 

• S comes next: Pope Leo X secures his release and he retires to San Casciano.

 

• R closes it: "his life at this period" (the retirement) is described in a letter, and the letter explains why he wrote "The Prince".

◦ Correct order: Q → P → S → R (QPSR).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (PQRS): wrong — P ("Shortly after this") cannot come first, as "this" has no reference.

 

• Option 2 (RQPS): wrong — R ("at this period") cannot come first, since the period has not yet been described.

 

• Option 3 (SPRQ): wrong — S (his release) cannot come before the arrest in P, and the dismissal in Q must precede all of these. (The PDF shows this option as a wrong selection.)

 

NOTE

 

• Tip: look for the sentence that introduces the subject (Q), then for linking phrases such as "shortly after this" (P) and "at this period" (R).

question:
A sentence has been divided into four fragments. From the options provided, identify the fragment that contains a grammatical error.

National liberation struggles/were driving with a diverse/range of radical, reformist,/and Marxist ideologies.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. were driving with a diverse.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The error is in "were driving with a diverse". Struggles are "driven by" ideologies (passive voice with "by"), so the sentence should read: "National liberation struggles were driven by a diverse range of radical, reformist, and Marxist ideologies."

◦ Rule: the doer/cause of the force is introduced with "by", not "with".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "National liberation struggles" is correct — it is a plural subject.

 

• Option 3: "range of radical, reformist," is correct — "a diverse range of" is a proper phrase.

 

• Option 4: "and Marxist ideologies." is correct — it completes the list.

 

NOTE

 

• Similar: driven by (not driven with); motivated by; inspired by.

question:
In the following sentence, four parts are given. Choose the part that contains a grammatical error.

The proposal which the board/approved after several revisions/are likely to improve/the admission process significantly.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. are likely to improve.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The error is in "are likely to improve". The subject is the singular noun "proposal" ("which the board approved after several revisions" is only a describing clause), so the verb must be singular: "is likely to improve".

◦ Corrected sentence: The proposal which the board approved after several revisions is likely to improve the admission process significantly.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "The proposal which the board" is correct — it begins the relative clause.

 

• Option 2: "approved after several revisions" is correct — the past tense verb is right.

 

• Option 4: "the admission process significantly." is correct — it is a proper object with an adverb.

 

NOTE

 

• Rule: do not be misled by the nearest noun ("revisions"); the verb agrees with the real subject ("proposal").

question:
Select the most appropriate option to improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

The advisor, as well as the assistants, were responsible for checking the final health advisory.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. was responsible.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• With "as well as", the verb agrees with the first subject. Here the subject is the singular "advisor", so the verb must be singular: "was responsible".

◦ Corrected sentence: The advisor, as well as the assistants, was responsible for checking the final health advisory.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: are responsibles is wrong — "responsible" is an adjective and has no plural form, and "are" is plural.

 

• Option 3: were being responsible is wrong — it is plural and an awkward continuous form.

 

• Option 4: have responsible is wrong — "have" cannot be followed by the adjective "responsible".

 

• The PDF shows Option 1 as a wrong selection.

 

NOTE

 

• "as well as", "along with", "together with", "in addition to": the verb agrees with the first subject.

question:
Complete the following passage by filling in the blanks with the most appropriate words from the options given below.

 

The prospect of "de-extinction" has moved from the realm of (A)____ science fiction to the high-tech laboratory, yet the moral landscape governing such ventures remains profoundly ambiguous. While the ability to sequence ancient DNA is a marvel of modern genomics, the ethical framework required to manage the consequences is still in its infancy. We are, in essence, attempting to rewrite natural history without a full grasp of the original narrative.

 

While the technical prowess required to revive a species is immense, the ecological ramifications are even more significant. Introducing a long-lost herbivore into a modern ecosystem could trigger a trophic (B)____ that shifts the entire balance of local flora and fauna. These environments have evolved for millennia in the absence of such creatures, and a sudden reintroduction could be more disruptive than restorative.

 

There is also a significant opportunity cost associated with these "vanity" projects. Critics argue that we might better spend our finite resources on protecting extant species that are currently facing (C)____ threats of extinction. Diverting funds toward the resurrection of the woolly mammoth may inadvertently accelerate the demise of the living elephant species we still have left.

 

Furthermore, the reintroduced species might find itself a "biological orphan", bereft (D)____ the social structures and environmental cues it once thrived upon. A mammoth born to a surrogate elephant mother would lack the ancestral knowledge of migration patterns and social hierarchies. It would be a creature displaced in time, existing as a lonely curiosity rather than a functional member of a biological community.

 

Ultimately, the question is not whether we possess the genetic tools to reach into the past, but whether we ought to proceed. Just because a scientific "could" exists doesn't (E)____ a moral "should" follows. We must decide if our role is to be the restorers of the past or the responsible guardians of the present.

 

Fill in the blank (A) with the correct word selecting from the given alternatives.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. speculative.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The blank comes before the noun phrase "science fiction", so an adjective is needed: speculative (काल्पनिक / अनुमानित) — based on imagination or guesswork rather than fact. "Speculative science fiction" is a common phrase.

◦ Correct: The prospect of "de-extinction" has moved from the realm of speculative science fiction to the high-tech laboratory.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: speculator (सट्टेबाज़) is a noun (a person who speculates), which cannot describe "science fiction".

 

• Option 3: speculated is a verb form (past tense), which does not fit before a noun. (The PDF shows this option as a wrong selection.)

 

• Option 4: speculation (अटकल) is a noun; "speculation science fiction" is not grammatical.

 

NOTE

 

• Word forms: speculate (verb), speculation (noun), speculator (person), speculative (adjective).

Which word best completes the scientific term in blank (B) to describe the ecological phenomenon mentioned?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. cascade.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The scientific term is trophic cascade (पोषी सोपानी प्रभाव): a chain of effects through the food web that starts when a species (here, a predator or herbivore) is added or removed and changes the balance of the whole ecosystem.

• Option 1: siphoning (सिफ़न से खींचना) means drawing off liquid, which is not an ecological term here.

NOTE

 

• "Cascade" means a series of events, each caused by the one before.

solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. mean.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• After the auxiliary doesn't (does not), the base form of the verb is used. So the correct word is mean: "Just because a scientific 'could' exists doesn't mean a moral 'should' follows."

◦ Rule: does/doesn't + base verb (V1).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: means is wrong: after "doesn't" the verb does not take the "-s" form.

 

• Option 3: meant is wrong: it is the past form and cannot follow "doesn't".

 

• Option 4: meaning is wrong: the "-ing" form does not follow "doesn't" here.

 

NOTE

 

• Remember: does not + V1 (He does not know), did not + V1 (He did not know).
